findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts whenever the member count divides evenly by the page size. With 50 members and limit 50, it reports 2 pages although there is only one. The 'next' arrow stays enabled, so clicking it sets offset=50 and fetches an empty page. Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` with `totalPages`, the pager also shows '1/2' on the real last page. The same stale count shows up after `removeMember`: deleting the only member on the last page reloads using the old `user_count` and leaves an empty page. This should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI
findings.body: `members` now defaults to `limit = 50` for every group, where before only automatic groups were limited, to 200. The public `group/members.hbs` template renders `members` but has no next/previous controls, and `group-members.js.es6` only calls `model.findMembers()` once with the default offset. Any group with more than 50 members now shows only the first 50 on its public page, and users cannot reach the rest. Pagination was added only to the admin UI.

findings.title: GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from an array to {members, meta} without updating specs
findings.body: The endpoint used to return a JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`. Any other consumer of this endpoint, such as plugins, external API clients or existing specs for `GroupsController#members`, will break. The PR adds no spec for the new response format or for limit/offset behaviour. The only spec changes are for the admin controller, so the changed public contract has no test coverage.

findings.title: limit and offset are not validated or capped
findings.body: `limit` and `offset` come straight from `params` via `to_i`. A negative value makes Postgres raise "LIMIT must not be negative" or an equivalent offset error, which returns a 500. A very large `limit` lets any user who can see the group pull the entire member list in one request, so the pagination does not bound the cost. The values should be clamped, for example 1..N for limit and >=0 for offset.

findings.title: add_members silently ignores unknown usernames and assumes a string param
findings.body: Usernames that do not match a user are skipped and the action still returns `success_json`. The admin gets no signal that nothing was added, and the UI just reloads the unchanged list. Usernames are also not stripped, so `"a, b"` silently drops `b`. If `usernames` arrives as an array, `.split` raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. The client also never clears the selector (the code has a `TODO: should clear the input`), so the admin can click Add repeatedly with the same input.

findings.title: Incremental PATCH membership API and usernames on create/update removed outright
findings.body: `update_patch` (PATCH with `changes[add]`/`changes[delete]`) is deleted. `create` and `update` no longer accept `group[usernames]`, and the params are now top-level rather than nested under `group`. Any external script or plugin using the old admin endpoints breaks with no deprecation path. The old specs for these behaviours were deleted rather than ported.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb and coverage is thin
findings.body: The route is `delete "members"`, but the automatic-group test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`. It passes only because controller specs do not enforce the verb, and it misrepresents the real request. The remove/add specs also never cover removing a non-member (where `group.users.delete(id)` raises RecordNotFound), adding unknown usernames, or non-admin access.
